photos.observed: Live ballyhoo swimming over sand in clear shallow water (Cuba), full side view: long needle-like lower jaw with dark tip, short upper jaw, slender silvery body, upper tail lobe yellow-orange, lower lobe paler.
photos.basis: Halfbeak with elongated lower jaw only; yellow-orange upper caudal lobe distinguishes ballyhoo from balao (McBride et al. 1996).
photos.use: Anatomy and colours of the bait fish. Bait ballyhoo is dead and rigged: do not show it swimming freely on its own; no hook or leader visible here. File is the standard-size Wikimedia thumbnail (downscaled, not cropped) because originals were rate-limited.

photos.observed: Close top view of a male blue crab on white shells (Louisiana): olive-green carapace front with marginal teeth and long lateral spine, bright blue claws with dark tips, blue legs. Rear of the carapace cut off by the frame.
photos.basis: Olive carapace with marginal teeth ending in a strong lateral spine and bright blue claws (Chesapeake Bay Program marks).
photos.use: Colour and shell details for blue crab bait pieces. Shows a whole live crab, not a halved bait: do not copy the shell bed background. File is the standard-size Wikimedia thumbnail (downscaled, not cropped) because originals were rate-limited.

photos.observed: Several whole raw chicken livers on a wooden cutting board: glossy dark red-maroon lobes, soft wet surface, small pale connective tissue bits
photos.basis: Raw chicken liver lobes (described by uploader as raw liver being prepared) - colour and wet gloss of the bait material
photos.use: Material/colour reference before cutting into chunks; not hooked and not hardened (S3) - bait chunks are smaller pieces

photos.observed: Two rusty crayfish on a silty shallow bottom seen through clear water; reddish-brown carapaces, banded tails, greenish claws, one facing the camera with claws spread
photos.basis: Live crayfish in natural shallow water; rust-coloured carapace and claws of Faxonius rusticus named by photographer (Ontario)
photos.use: Reference for how live crayfish sit and look underwater from above; invasive in many US waters - check legality before showing as live bait

photos.observed: Virile crayfish photographed from above on white: two large speckled claws with pale tips, antennae, smooth carapace, segmented abdomen ending in tail fan, walking legs
photos.basis: Freshwater crayfish body plan: chelae, carapace, segmented tail with fan; species Faxonius (Orconectes) virilis named by SERC, 89 mm carapace length
photos.use: Identity/anatomy of a whole native US crayfish; this individual is large (89 mm CL) - do not use for bait scale; not hooked; whole-live and tail-meat variants derive from this anatomy

photos.observed: Focus-stacked macro of a house cricket head and forelegs: tan-brown body, large black compound eye, very long ringed antennae, spiny legs
photos.basis: House cricket (Acheta domesticus, a commonly sold feeder cricket) named by photographer; long antennae and tan colour typical of cricket
photos.use: Head/antenna detail only; whole-body shape and hind jumping legs not shown; not hooked

photos.observed: Two differential grasshoppers (mating pair) on a leaf stem in Ohio: olive-yellow bodies, short antennae, enlarged hind femurs with black chevron marks, folded wings
photos.basis: Short antennae, large jumping hind legs and wings folded over abdomen identify a grasshopper (Melanoplus differentialis, named by photographer)
photos.use: Identity of a US field grasshopper; mating pair - show a single insect in bait scenes; not hooked

photos.credit: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Northeast Region), public domain
photos.observed: USFWS biologist on a boat holding a live American eel in gloved hands, body curving; olive-brown back, pale belly, long continuous dorsal fin, small pectoral fin.
photos.basis: Snake-like live eel with one continuous fin from back around the tail; species named in USFWS caption (Osage River).
photos.use: Body shape, colour and curling posture of a live eel. Large wild eel, not a hooked bait: do not copy the size, the person, the USFWS cap logo or the boat. File is the standard-size Wikimedia thumbnail (downscaled, not cropped) because originals were rate-limited.

photos.observed: Live hellgrammite on wet stream gravel and slate, top view: dark brown flattened head and thorax plates, segmented abdomen with paired pointed lateral filaments along both sides, hooked tail appendages
photos.basis: Long flattened body, head with mandibles, 8 pairs of pointed lateral abdominal appendages as in MDC description (S8); captioned as dobsonfly larva from a Tennessee stream
photos.use: Identity of the hellgrammite bait insect in natural setting; colours oversaturated by camera - use MDC colours (dark brown/tan/black); not hooked

photos.credit: Donald Trung Quoc Don (Chữ Hán: 徵國單) - Wikimedia Commons - © CC BY-SA 4.0 International.(Want to use this image?)Original publication 📤: --Donald Trung 『徵國單』 (No Fake News 💬) (WikiProject Numismatics 💴) (Articles 📚) 08:40, 23 September 2020 (UTC)
photos.observed: Small green tub held in a hand, full of pale off-white fly maggots (fishing maggots) dusted with sawdust/bran
photos.basis: Uploader states a box of maggots for fishing; legless tapered pale larvae typical of spikes
photos.use: Identity of bait maggots/spikes in bulk; photographed in the Netherlands - US spikes look the same but may be dyed; do not copy the tub branding (none visible)

photos.observed: Many Tenebrio molitor larvae in oat bedding: shiny golden-brown cylindrical segmented bodies with darker segment bands, plus a pale freshly molted larva/pupa and shed skins
photos.basis: Hard, glossy, banded yellow-brown segments and three small legs near the head - typical mealworm larvae; species named by photographer (Tenebrio molitor)
photos.use: Identity of mealworm colour/segments; the pale soft individual is a fresh moult or pupa - do not use as normal bait colour; not hooked

photos.observed: Focus-stacked side view of a single wax moth caterpillar on black: soft pale cream-yellow segmented body, sparse fine hairs, small dark spiracle dots, brown head capsule, short legs
photos.basis: Galleria mellonella larva (the waxworm) named by USGS photographer; soft cream body with brown head typical of bait waxworms
photos.use: Identity of a waxworm; wild specimen from a bumble bee nest, bait-shop waxworms look the same; not on a jig

photos.credit: Robert Aguilar, Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (Flickr), CC BY 2.0
photos.observed: Whole juvenile Atlantic menhaden (106 mm SL) on a grey background, left side view: silvery deep body, large head and eye, one black shoulder spot behind the gill cover, yellowish forked tail.
photos.basis: Single distinct black shoulder spot behind the gill opening on a silvery deep-bodied herring-like fish (NOAA identification mark).
photos.use: Identity of a small menhaden (peanut/pogy size) as used for live or cut bait. Lab specimen, not hooked and not swimming; do not copy the grey background.

photos.observed: Dead adult menhaden lying on wet beach sand, photographed from above showing its side: shoulder spot followed by a row of smaller dark spots, iridescent blue-silver back, yellow tail; gill area and mouth damaged.
photos.basis: Black shoulder spot plus a row of smaller spots behind it on a deep silvery body; yellow caudal fin.
photos.use: Adult spot pattern and colour for whole/cut bunker. Stranded, damaged fish: do not copy the torn gills or sand for fresh bait. File is the standard-size Wikimedia thumbnail (downscaled, not cropped) because originals were rate-limited.

photos.observed: Creek chub on white background, side view, olive-silver body with dusky lateral band, rounded snout, single dorsal fin; no hook
photos.basis: Fish identified as creek chub by USFWS photographer; chubs are a pike bait (S7)
photos.use: Identity of a chub-type bait minnow; hooking not shown; creek chub can grow to 10 in - match bait size to scene from size table

photos.observed: Fresh adult emerald shiner specimen on white background, slender silvery body, large eye, thin olive back, silver lateral stripe; no hook
photos.basis: Slender silver shiner body named by USFWS as emerald shiner (Missouri River, SD); emerald shiner is a Minnesota bait shiner (S8)
photos.use: Identity of an emerald shiner as bait fish; hooking not shown - apply variant hook position from profile; studio white background, do not copy

photos.observed: Breeding-male fathead minnow in an aquarium over pebbles: blunt dark head with nuptial tubercles on snout, dark lateral stripe, dusky banded dorsal fin, orange-tinged belly
photos.basis: Blunt rounded head, short deep body and dark-spotted dorsal of fathead minnow, named by photographer; breeding-male colours
photos.use: Identity of fathead minnow; breeding male colours and tubercles are seasonal - typical bait fatheads are plainer olive-silver; no hook shown

photos.credit: Robert Aguilar, Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (Flickr), CC BY 2.0
photos.observed: Whole small white mullet (Mugil curema, 68 mm SL) on a pale background, left side view: silvery cylindrical body, blunt head, large scales, two separate dorsal fins, forked pale tail.
photos.basis: Mullet body plan (blunt head, two widely separated dorsal fins, large scales); 68 mm SL is finger-mullet size (2-4 in).
photos.use: Identity and size class of a finger mullet. Lab specimen, not live and not hooked; does not show a cut chunk. Do not copy the background.

photos.credit: Hester Eugene, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
photos.observed: Bluegill lifted from water with a pink earthworm on a small hook at its mouth; line runs straight up; worm body hangs in loops with free ends dangling
photos.basis: Single fine-wire hook enters the worm near the top, worm ends dangle free below the hook, so most of the worm hangs instead of being threaded along the shank (S2)
photos.use: Assembly reference: one hook, worm hooked once/twice with ends dangling; worm looks smaller than a full adult crawler - do not use for scale; fish is a bluegill

photos.observed: Two live Lumbricus terrestris on wet dead leaves and soil, glossy pink-brown segmented bodies, darker front, paler flattened tail end
photos.basis: Large ringed earthworm body, many fine segments, front darker and tail paler/flattened as described for nightcrawler (S4); species named by photographer
photos.use: Identity of the live nightcrawler body (colour, segments, gloss); no hook shown; photographed in Denmark, same species as US bait crawlers

photos.credit: United States Fish and Wildlife Services
photos.observed: Three small gizzard shad of different sizes on an open wet palm above a deck, green bucket nearby; deep silvery bodies, dark spot behind the gill cover, yellow eye, forked tail
photos.basis: Deep compressed silver body with dark shoulder spot - gizzard shad, captioned as native fish by USFWS (title 'Gizzard shad')
photos.use: Identity of whole gizzard shad (young fish) before cutting or live use; adults used as cut bait are larger; no hook shown

photos.credit: Robert Aguilar, Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (Flickr), CC BY 2.0
photos.observed: One whole white shrimp (Litopenaeus setiferus, 68 mm) on a black background, side view: translucent speckled body, rostrum over the eye, very long red-brown antennae, walking and swimming legs, red-edged tail fan. Not on a hook.
photos.basis: Penaeid shrimp marks: toothed rostrum (horn) above the eye, segmented curved abdomen, tail fan, long antennae; 68 mm is within the 2-4 in live-bait range.
photos.use: Shape, translucency and anatomy of a live penaeid bait shrimp (where the horn and tail are). Not hooked: do not use for hook position. Do not copy the black studio background. File is the standard-size Wikimedia thumbnail (downscaled, not cropped) because originals were rate-limited.

photos.credit: NOAA/NMFS SEFSC Pascagoula Laboratory (collection of Brandi Noble), public domain
photos.observed: One whole longfin inshore squid lying on a pale surface: reddish speckled tubular mantle, triangular fins at the mantle tip, large eye, short arms and two long tentacles with clubs.
photos.basis: Tubular mantle with long rear fins, 8 arms plus 2 longer tentacles: a whole loliginid squid as sold for bait.
photos.use: Whole squid shape and colour. Not hooked and not cut into strips; do not copy the background. File is the standard-size Wikimedia thumbnail (downscaled, not cropped) because originals were rate-limited.

photos.observed: Adult white sucker in an aquarium over sand, side view; long round body, olive-brassy back and sides, lower fins pale, blunt snout with mouth on the underside
photos.basis: Lower horizontal (subterminal) mouth and brassy/greenish sides match MDC white sucker description (S5); titled white sucker by USFWS
photos.use: Identity of the bait species; this is an adult display fish, larger than 2-6 in walleye bait - use size table; no hook or rig shown

photos.observed: White sucker swimming above gravel and driftwood in a tank; slim olive body, pale belly, small eye, fleshy lips under the snout
photos.basis: Subterminal mouth with fleshy lips and olive-silver body consistent with S5; species named by photographer
photos.use: Second identity reference (CC BY 2.0, credit Brian Gratwicke); no hook or rig shown

photos.observed: Four hard crankbaits on white background, side view: two small round-bill crankbaits, a crawfish-pattern medium crankbait, and at the bottom a fat shad-pattern crankbait with a long clear bill; each has two treble hooks (belly and tail).
photos.basis: Bottom lure: long transparent bill about half the body length with line-tie loop on the bill, compact belly body, two trebles = deep-diving crankbait; the others show short bills (shallow divers).
photos.use: Identity of long-bill deep diver and comparison with short-bill crankbaits; brand text on bodies, do not copy logo/text.

photos.observed: Eleven hard lures on white: bottom-left a large flat-sided lipless crankbait with gold scale finish, line-tie rings on the back and two trebles; other lures are lipped crankbaits and minnow jerkbaits.
photos.basis: Bottom-left lure: no bill, deep laterally compressed body, line-tie on top of the back behind the head, two trebles = lipless crankbait.
photos.use: Use only the bottom-left lure as lipless reference; rest of frame shows other types.

photos.observed: Two crankbaits on white: top a red-headed fat crankbait with short clear round bill, belly and tail trebles; bottom a jointed three-section crankbait with a long clear bill.
photos.basis: Top lure: short rounded clear bill, compact deep body, two trebles = round-bill shallow/medium crankbait. Bottom lure is a jointed long-bill diver (not a target variant).
photos.use: Identity for shallow-diver (top lure); bottom jointed lure is not a reference for any variant here; small model text on bottom lure, do not copy logo/text.

photos.observed: Hair-wing dry fly held in a red fly-tying vise on a dark blue background: long stiff tail fibres, grey dubbed body, upright hair wing and a dense collar of brown and grizzly hackle fibres radiating around the hook shank behind the eye.
photos.basis: Stiff tail plus full radiating hackle collar and upright wing on a single hook, built to sit on the surface film: dry fly.
photos.use: Identity and anatomy of a classic dry fly. Do not copy the vise or studio background; in scenes the fly floats on the surface. File is the Wikimedia Commons standard rendition of the original (downscaled, not cropped); original download was rate-limited.

photos.observed: Bead-head nymph in a vise on teal background: metal bead at the eye, short brown hackle legs, two white biot wings lying back over a peacock-herl body, forked brown biot tail.
photos.basis: Compact slim body with metal bead head and short legs on a single hook, no floating hackle collar: bead-head nymph (Prince type).
photos.use: Identity and anatomy of a bead-head nymph. Do not copy the vise or background; in scenes it drifts below the surface near the bottom. File is the Wikimedia Commons standard rendition of the original (downscaled, not cropped); original download was rate-limited.

photos.observed: Small red fly-rod popping bug held in a vise on light blue background: hard red head with a cupped (concave) face and painted yellow-black eye, red and grizzly hackle collar and tail fibres behind it, long red-black striped rubber legs hanging down.
photos.basis: Hard floating head with cupped face, rubber legs and hackle on a single hook, much smaller than a topwater plug and with no treble: popping bug.
photos.use: Identity and anatomy of a fly-rod popping bug. Do not copy the vise or background; foam spiders (also in this variant) look different: soft foam body, no cupped face. File is the Wikimedia Commons standard rendition of the original (downscaled, not cropped); original download was rate-limited.

photos.observed: Black woolly bugger in a vise on red background: long black marabou tail longer than the hook, black chenille body with palmered black hackle, small orange thread head at the eye.
photos.basis: Long flowing tail and palmered body making a fish/leech profile longer than the hook: streamer (woolly bugger).
photos.use: Identity of a woolly-bugger streamer. Do not copy vise or background. File is the Wikimedia Commons standard rendition of the original (downscaled, not cropped); original download was rate-limited.

photos.observed: Yellow and red bucktail streamer lying on a wooden board: silver ribbed body, layered yellow and red hair wing sweeping back past the hook bend, glossy black thread head.
photos.basis: Long hair wing extending past the hook bend over a slim tinsel body, baitfish profile: bucktail streamer (Mickey Finn pattern).
photos.use: Identity of a hair-wing baitfish streamer, no vise. Not a bucktail jig: there is no lead head. File is the Wikimedia Commons standard rendition of the original (downscaled, not cropped); original download was rate-limited.

photos.observed: Alexandra wet fly in a vise on dark blue background: silver tinsel body, red tail, slender wing of peacock sword fibres swept low back over the body with red strips, black thread head; no radiating hackle collar.
photos.basis: Wing laid back along the body and no bushy floating hackle: classic winged wet fly fished below the surface.
photos.use: Identity of a classic winged wet fly. Wet-fly construction is not described by an A/B source; do not copy vise or background. File is the Wikimedia Commons standard rendition of the original (downscaled, not cropped); original download was rate-limited.

photos.observed: Two bare ball jigheads with single hooks and a ribbed soft plastic curly-tail grub threaded onto a ball jighead, hook point exiting the back, sickle-shaped tail curling up.
photos.basis: Ribbed short body with thin sickle-shaped curly tail, threaded on a round lead jighead with one single hook = curly-tail grub on jighead.
photos.use: Identity and rigging reference (body tight to head, hook exits back).

photos.observed: Two soft plastic baits on white: lower a translucent glitter grub with ribbed body and single curly tail; upper a yellow double-tail grub.
photos.basis: Lower bait: ribbed body with one sickle curly tail, no hook = unrigged curly-tail grub; upper double-tail is a related form outside the variants.
photos.use: Identity for unrigged single curly-tail grub (lower bait).

photos.observed: Two small inline spinners on a white surface: left has a willow-shaped printed blade on a clevis above a fish-head body, right has a rounder printed blade on a clevis above a brass bullet body; both end in a treble dressed with red fibres; wire loop line tie at the top of each straight shaft.
photos.basis: Blade mounted on a clevis that turns around a straight wire shaft, weighted body behind the blade, single treble at the end: standard inline spinner.
photos.use: Identity and anatomy of small trout-size inline spinners (shaft, clevis, blade, body, dressed treble). Printed blade patterns are not to be copied exactly. File is the Wikimedia Commons standard rendition of the original (downscaled, not cropped); original download was rate-limited.

photos.observed: Single inline spinner hanging from its line against a blurred green background: gold oval blade with black dots on a clevis at the front of a straight wire shaft, brass beads and a ribbed brass body with red bands below it, bare treble at the bottom, wire loop and swivel above.
photos.basis: Blade on clevis beside a straight shaft, weighted body behind it, one treble at the end: standard inline spinner (French-type blade).
photos.use: Identity and anatomy of a classic French-blade inline spinner hanging at rest (blade hangs beside the shaft when not pulled). Do not copy the brand name and size number printed on the blade. File is the Wikimedia Commons standard rendition of the original (downscaled, not cropped); original download was rate-limited.

photos.observed: Single gold-and-orange slim balsa-style minnow lure with short clear bill, belly and tail trebles, attached by snap swivel to line, on grey wood.
photos.basis: Slim minnow body, small clear bill at nose, two trebles, nose line tie = minnow jerkbait/stickbait; buoyancy class not visible.
photos.use: Type identity; snap-swivel on line is optional hardware, not part of the lure; brand model, do not copy any brand marking.

photos.observed: Four long slim minnow-shaped hard lures with small clear bills, two or three treble hooks each, side view on white; top one shorter with a slightly longer bill.
photos.basis: Long thin minnow bodies several times longer than deep, small short bills at the nose, belly/tail trebles = minnow jerkbait/twitchbait; floating vs suspending not visible.
photos.use: Type identity only (variant not determinable from a still photo); small text on bodies, do not copy logo/text.

photos.observed: Two bare ball jigheads (round lead head molded on a single hook, one with a separate wide-gap hook on a ring) plus three curly-tail grubs, one rigged on a ball jighead.
photos.basis: Round lead head molded onto the shank of a single hook with line-tie eye on top = plain ball jighead.
photos.use: Anatomy of ball jighead; the grubs belong to EQP-LURE-GRUB.

photos.credit: R. Henrik Nilsson / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
photos.observed: Foam-lined box with rows of tiny metal teardrop-shaped jigs in silver, copper and brass finishes, each with a small single hook; a few painted bead jigs at top right.
photos.basis: Small drop-shaped metal bodies with a hole and tiny single hook = teardrop ice jigs (European mormyshka, same form).
photos.use: Identity for teardrop ice jig; scale is tiny, do not enlarge to bass size.

photos.observed: Fluorescent orange banana-shaped plug lying on its side in front of its vintage cardboard box; curved one-piece body with a broad flat head (right) and no separate diving lip; one treble hangs from the belly and one from the tail on screw eyes.
photos.basis: Curved banana body with broad flat forehead acting as the diving face, two trebles under the body: banana plug (Flatfish type).
photos.use: Identity of the banana-plug shape and treble positions. Do not copy the box, brand name or text; the box is not part of the lure. File is the Wikimedia Commons standard rendition of the original (downscaled, not cropped); original download was rate-limited.

photos.observed: Five bass lures laid on a light surface: a short-bill crankbait, a chrome lipless rattle bait, a blue creature bait, a green curly-tailed lizard, and at the right a dark straight soft plastic stick worm with no tail or appendages.
photos.basis: Rightmost bait: straight, slightly tapered dark soft plastic cylinder with rounded ends, no curly tail, legs or hook = unrigged soft stick worm (senko-style).
photos.use: Use only the rightmost bait for soft-stick; slightly soft focus; other lures belong to other profiles.

photos.observed: Spinnerbait on white: bent wire safety-pin frame, upper arm carrying a small round blade and a large willow blade, lower arm with painted lead head with eye, green/white silicone skirt hiding a single upturned hook.
photos.basis: V-shaped wire frame, two blades (small Colorado/Indiana + long pointed willow) on the upper arm, head + skirt + one single hook on the lower arm = tandem willow spinnerbait.
photos.use: Identity for tandem-willow; shows correct blade-above-head geometry.

photos.observed: Small brass-gold teardrop spoon on a white surface, convex back facing camera; treble hook hangs from a split ring at the wide tail with a small red bead; split ring and barrel swivel at the narrow nose; text stamped on the blade.
photos.basis: One curved metal blade with no shaft or rotating blade, treble on split ring at tail, line tie at nose: casting spoon.
photos.use: Identity of a small casting spoon and its split-ring/treble/swivel connections. Do not copy the stamped text on the blade.

photos.observed: Copper oval spoon with a ribbed (wave-pressed) front half on a white background; barrel swivel and split ring at the nose, split ring at the tail carrying a pink plastic tag and a treble hook.
photos.basis: Single curved metal blade, no shaft or spinning blade, treble on split ring at the tail, swivel at the nose: casting spoon.
photos.use: Identity and connection details of a casting spoon (swivel, split rings, tag, treble). Pressed rib pattern is one finish among many. File is the Wikimedia Commons standard rendition of the original (downscaled, not cropped); original download was rate-limited.

photos.observed: Dark metal weedless spoon lying on a rock at a lake edge, seen from the side; split ring and barrel swivel at the nose; a fixed upturned hook riveted at the tail on the concave side; a thin wire weed guard rises from a front rivet toward the hook point.
photos.basis: Single curved metal blade (spoon), one fixed hook instead of a treble, wire weed guard covering the hook point: weedless spoon.
photos.use: Identity and anatomy of the weedless spoon (fixed hook plus wire guard, split ring at nose). Product label from Commons title (BETE Nix-draget) is not to be copied; scale is not measured from the photo. File is the Wikimedia Commons standard rendition of the original (downscaled, not cropped); original download was rate-limited.

photos.observed: Three hard multi-jointed swimbaits with realistic sunfish, bass and trout paint: segmented bodies with visible joint gaps, two treble hooks each, nose line-tie, fish-shaped tails.
photos.basis: Hard bodies divided into several hinged segments, realistic fish shape, two trebles = hard multi-jointed swimbait.
photos.use: Identity for hard-multi-joint; uploaded by the maker, no logo visible.

photos.observed: Two soft plastic shad-shaped baits with paddle tails rigged on lead jigheads (round and fish-head shapes), hook points exiting the back; embossed brand lettering on the plastic.
photos.basis: Fish-shaped soft body ending in a flat paddle tail set across the body, jighead at the nose with single hook = paddletail swimbait on jighead.
photos.use: Identity and rigging reference; embossed brand on plastic, do not copy logo/text.

photos.observed: Soft rainbow-trout-like swimbait with paddle tail, molded fins, top line-tie, single hook point exiting the back and a small treble under the belly, on wood.
photos.basis: Soft realistic fish body ending in paddle tail, internal weight/hook with hook exiting the back = pre-rigged paddletail swimbait.
photos.use: Identity for a large pre-rigged paddletail (muskie/bass scale).

photos.observed: Two popper plugs on dark slate: hard bodies with large concave open mouths at the nose, belly treble and feathered rear treble.
photos.basis: Cupped/concave face at nose, floating plug body, two trebles with feather dressing on the tail treble = popper/chugger.
photos.use: Identity for popper.

photos.observed: Two surface lures on white: top a white popper with concave face and feathered tail treble; bottom an orange-yellow cigar-shaped stickbait with rounded nose, nose line tie, belly and tail trebles, no bill.
photos.basis: Bottom lure: long cigar body without lip or cup, eye at nose, two trebles = walk-the-dog pencil/stickbait; top lure shows popper cupped face for contrast.
photos.use: Identity for walk-the-dog (bottom lure); brand text on popper, do not copy logo/text.
